findings.finding: [PARKED 2026-08-17 by the owner — contributions are not open to anyone right now, so a command nobody can act on is not worth a redesign yet.] plugin/commands/contribute.md (SHIPPED) is still built on the dead two-tree model: it stages domains/<name>/plugin/{skills,library}/ and its scope-safety rule forbids staging plugin/ (CORE) — but promote-run.js locate() lands promotions in plugin/{skills,library}/ (one tree). findings.finding: ui/server/features/skills/skill-scope.js (+ skill-scope.check.js) still models the godot {genre, style} game-profile filter with godot-* skill examples baked into comments and the check fixtures (godot-core, style-pixel, genre-fps). findings.finding: [PARKED 2026-08-17 by the owner — the /epic pilot is deferred. The WIRING fix landed (c2cef8a), so the capability is reachable whenever the pilot happens.] RE-SCOPED 2026-08-16 against artifacts, not assumptions. The row claimed the whole 2026-07-30 wave was unproven; half of it is DONE: product-owner + the PRD contract have real runs (design/262-public-account-deletion-page.md, 248-, 247- on the bound project) and grill mode has driven live form sequences. The xeno-epic TOOL is the unproven half — and NOT because the gh path is broken: all 10 epic-labelled issues on the project are hand-rolled (no `Open decisions` / `Not yet specified` sections) and design/epics/ never existed, i.e. the tool was never REACHABLE. findings.pattern: a capability is reachable only when some layer ROUTES to it — frontmatter grants the tool, the prompt has to say when to reach for it.

findings.finding: Xenomoon now diverges from xenodot on more than identity: renamed roster (product-owner), fork-only tools (mcp__ui__epic), fork-only skills (grill, xeno-epic), fork-only process docs (skill-writing). No systematic check that these divergent surfaces are wired everywhere xenodot's originals were (hooks matchers, skill-catalog derivations, templates, first-boot copy, /sync-upstream seam list) — each landed by hand-grep. Add the fork-divergent surfaces to docs/fork/SEAMS.md so /sync-upstream and the audit suite treat them as first-class seams instead of rediscovering them per session. FIRST LIVE BITE (2026-07-30, fixed 376c614): trunk tracked plugin/library/sources/skill-sources.md — a path webapp-pack installs WRITE untracked — breaking `xenomoon update` in every bound clone; invariant extracted: the trunk never tracks a path a domain-pack install writes (audit should CHECK trunk-tracked paths against every pack's install file list).
findings.pattern: every fork-divergent surface is a named seam in SEAMS.md — sync and audit read the list, not the diff.

findings.finding: Nothing carries the human's OBJECTIVE across turns, so each turn re-derives its goal from the freshest thing in context. Observed live: 'close these issues' drifted to fix deploy -> fix gate -> fix red main -> reconcile branches, ending with 3 new PRs + 1 framework issue while open issues moved 24 -> 20. NOT a missing rule: ui/orchestrator-spine.md:73-74 already says 'Never silently expand scope … a change broader than the agreed slice → stop' and :15 says 'cut ONE small slice' — the prohibition exists and was violated, so restating it harder is the label-for-a-label move (cf. D8-qa-pass-not-bound-to-sha). The MECHANISM gap is precise: the only thing in the framework that holds an objective is Autonomous Mode (standing Main Goal in .xenomoon/autonomous.json, with check turns that RESTATE the goal every tick — autonomous-main-goal/SKILL.md:9), and it is heavyweight (must be armed, self-drives, and escalates permissions via session.autonomousActive). For a plain ask there is no lightweight equivalent. Precedent for the shape of a fix already exists in the spine: it has restate-discipline for EXECUTION SHAPE ('after a correction, restate the shape in one line before dispatching anything else') but nothing for OBJECTIVE. SECOND HALF: nothing anywhere measures CLOSURE — every loop we ship counts production (tasks created, promotions filed, findings logged, epics charted), so the generated-vs-closed ratio is invisible to every mechanism in the repo, and what is not measured does not get optimised. The fix is NOT another rule and NOT a fourth subsystem beside Autonomous/epics/Pulse — reaching for a new mechanism here would enact the very failure. Design first, like Pulse got. Candidate for the closure half only: a note-class Pulse check (see D9-pulse-amplifies-scope-drift) firing on a worsening ratio, since that is deterministic state over time and fits machinery that already exists.
findings.pattern: an objective the human stated is durable and restated before each dispatch — a prohibition against drifting is not a mechanism for holding the aim.

findings.finding: HYPOTHESIS, not a measurement — Pulse (02be9c9) has never run in a live armed session yet, and this must be judged from a real one before acting. The risk: Pulse is a LEAD GENERATOR. Every beat hands the orchestrator a fresh list of things that are not done, and its first live run surfaced exactly the items a scope-drift post-mortem got lost fixing (pr:273:blocked, pr:269:blocked). Given an orchestrator that converts discovery into new work (D6-objective-not-durable), a periodic injector of new discoveries may amplify the drift it was never meant to touch. The only thing standing against that today is PROSE — the spine's Pulse rule ('Reconcile only … no code, no refactor, no new slices') plus the same sentence in the beat turn. This session's own evidence says prose guards are weak: the terse rule was stated five different ways across 14 agents, two of them runtime loads that could silently never happen. Watch on the first armed session: does a beat terminate in landing/ask-filing, or does it spawn slices? If it spawns, make the guard mechanical rather than louder — e.g. a Pulse-turn tool envelope, or beats that carry only `act`/`ask` items and drop `note` entirely when the session already has open work. Related: the closure-metric idea from D6 would live here as a note-class check, and must not itself become a to-do generator.
findings.pattern: a mechanism that surfaces work must be judged on whether it ENDS work — a safety net that adds leads faster than they close is a fuel line.

findings.finding: EXPLAINED + HALF-FIXED 2026-08-18; what remains is one environment check. CAUSE: the observing session was NOT a web-UI server session. Its own post-mortem named `block-branch-create.sh` as one of 'the hooks that do exist' — that file exists NOWHERE in this forge (plugin/hooks/ ships block-destructive-{git,shell}.sh; webapp ships commit-gate/commit-label/dependency-gate/push-gate; expoapp ships none), so it was running under a different hook set, i.e. a terminal session with project-local hooks and no canUseTool. That is why `git switch` executed while ui-control.js orchestratorGate had denied it since c7ab206 — the gate was never in the loop. FIX APPLIED: plugin/hooks/block-main-loop-mutations.sh — role gate (agent_id absent = main loop), mutating git DENY, merge/promote (gh pr merge, issuekit pr merge / promote / branch prune --apply) ASK, read-only git + the rest of issuekit + all sub-agents untouched, add/commit carved out to the pack's commit-gate when installed. 26 branches exercised, all pass. REMAINING: our hooks only reach a session that LOADS this plugin (web UI automatically; terminal via `/plugin marketplace add` + `/plugin install`). The observed environment ships hooks we do not, so confirm the plugin is actually installed there — if it is not, this fix does not reach it and the gap is an INSTALL gap, not a code gap. Original row text below. UNEXPLAINED BYPASS — needs a repro before any fix. The main-loop mutating-git deny DOES exist and DOES cover `switch`: ui/server/core/ui-control.js orchestratorGate() denies Bash for agent === 'main' when GIT_MUTATE_RE matches, wired through session-permissions.js:65 preToolGate, landed c7ab206 (2026-08-01, 'mutating git denied for the main loop'). Yet the 2026-08-17 post-mortem that filed the now-deleted D8-spine-claims-git-deny-that-does-not-exist observed an orchestrator running `git switch` a dozen times in one session. Both cannot be true of the same session. Two candidate explanations, UNTESTED: (a) that session was a plain Claude Code CLI session on the bound project, not a UI-server session — the gate lives in canUseTool, which only exists in the server's SDK session, and ui/orchestrator-spine.md is likewise only loaded by config.js buildSystemPrompt, so a CLI session gets NEITHER the sentence nor the gate and the claim is simply out of scope there; (b) the gate ran and did not fire (agent field not 'main' for the main loop under some path, or the command shape dodged the regex — e.g. an `rtk`-prefixed form, a heredoc, or git invoked via a wrapper). RESOLVE BY EVIDENCE, not by adding a second layer: find the post-mortem's session log, check whether it was a server session, and grep the permission log for policy:'orchestrator-gate' entries around those git calls. If (a), the real gap is that CORE ships no main-loop git guard for CLI-bound sessions and the hook layer (plugin/hooks/block-destructive-git.sh, which is role-blind by design) is the only thing present there — decide then whether that is a gap worth a hook or an accepted scope boundary. If (b), it is a live gate defect and takes priority. Filed 2026-08-17 while applying the deleted row, whose premise ('no such deny exists') was FALSE — it audited plugin/hooks/ only and missed the permission layer.
findings.pattern: a contradiction between a post-mortem observation and the code is a measurement question first — find which session the observation came from before hardening anything.
